recentItems.title: What Really Killed Bruce Lee? | History's Greatest Mysteries (S2, E3)
recentItems.description:
Bruce Lee died suddenly in 1973 at just 32 years old, weeks before Enter the Dragon would make him a global superstar. His death was officially attributed to a fatal reaction to a painkiller—but decades of rumors have raised questions about poisoning, organized crime, secret health problems and possible foul play.

At the request of Bruce's brother Robert, former Hong Kong police detective Philip Chan reexamines previously unreleased records, witness accounts and Bruce Lee's autopsy to determine what really happened. History's Greatest Mysteries (S2, E3) follows the evidence toward a new explanation for the sudden death of one of the world's most iconic martial artists.

recentItems.title: Saladin at the Gates of Jerusalem: The Siege of 1187 | HISTORY This Week
recentItems.description:
September 20, 1187. It’s daytime outside the walls of Jerusalem. Saladin, the Sultan of Egypt, ponders his next attack. His troops encircle and lay siege to the city. They vastly outnumber the Crusader knights inside, and Saladin is on the cusp of a victory he never dreamed possible. But he has a problem. Balian of Ibelin leads the Crusader defenses within the city walls. He threatens to destroy Muslim holy sites if Saladin attacks. The Sultan must make a choice. One that will impact his legacy, the lives of thousands, and the future of Jerusalem. 

Special thanks to our guest, Dr. Suleiman Mourad, Professor of Religion at Smith College and author of Ibn Asakir of Damascus: Champion of Sunni Islam at the Time of the Crusades.
**This episode originally aired September 19, 2022.
